newsitem.title: USA: U.S. NRC announces management reorganization.
newsitem.headline: U.S. NRC announces management reorganization.

text.p: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission chairwoman Shirley Jackson announced a reorganization Monday of top NRC management, effective January 5.
Jackson also said Leonard Callan, who has been NRC's Region 4 administrator, will become executive director for operations, replacing James Taylor, who will retire.
Also retiring will be James Milhoan, deputy executive director for nuclear reactor regulation, regional operations and research; and Stewart Ebneter, regional administrator for NRC Region 2.

Jackson said the changes stem partly from "recent insights gained from issues associated with reactor facilities in the Northeast," where the NRC has been criticized for responding too slowly to safety problems.
Samuel Collins, currently deputy regional administrator of Region 4, the NRC's western office, was named as the new director of the Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation.
With the reorganization, the executive director for operations (EDO) will continue to report directly to the NRC chairman, but will have three deputies instead of two.

Named to the new deputy EDO positions were Hugh Thomspon for regulatory programs, Edward Jordan for regulatory effectiveness, program oversight, investigations and enforcement, and Patricia Norry for management support. All currently hold NRC posts.

The deputy executive for regulatory programs will be responsible for the Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation, the Office of Nuclear Materials Safety and Safeguards, the four regional offices,and the Office of State Programs.
The post of deputy executive for regulatory effectiveness is to evaluate programs, independent of offices with day-to-day regulatory responsibilities.
Responsibilities of chief financial officer, which had been held by the EDO, will be handled by a new officer, who will report to the EDO, Jackson said.
Another new position -- chief information officer -- also will report to the EDO.
Appointments to those two positions will be named soon, Jackson said.
